title: Lexington named
summary: In June 1775, a party of frontiersmen led by William McConnell camped at a spring on a branch of Elkhorn Creek, and when news of the April 19 fight at Lexington, Massachusetts, reached them, they named the place Lexington.
bodyMarkdown:
In early June 1775, a party of frontiersmen led by William McConnell was surveying land along the forks of Elkhorn Creek in what is now Fayette County. They camped near a "sinking spring" on a branch of the creek, a spot known today as McConnell Springs. While they were there, word reached them that colonists had fought British troops at Lexington, Massachusetts, on April 19, 1775.

The party named their campsite Lexington to honor that first battle of the American Revolution. They hoped a town would one day grow there. Danger of Indian attacks delayed permanent settlement for four years.

In 1779, Col. Robert Patterson and about 25 companions came from Fort Harrod and built a blockhouse near today's Main and Mill streets. Cabins and a stockade followed. The Virginia General Assembly established the town of Lexington on May 6, 1782. McConnell Springs is now a city park, marked by state historical marker 554.

Sources: [Kentucky Historical Society, Marker 554: Lexington Named](https://history.ky.gov/markers/lexington-named); [Friends of McConnell Springs, Lexington & McConnell Springs History](https://mcconnellsprings.org/history-lexington-mcconnell-frontier/)
